plainClarity.observation: The presentation and report both due tomorrow create a concrete conflict. The first dialogue offers a date trade-off. The second offers scope reduction or another drafter if both dates are fixed. The ending explicitly avoids promising extra time. artifactEvidence.excerpt: Your manager needs a presentation by tomorrow. You already have a report due then. Before you agree to both, try: “I can finish the presentation tomorrow, but the report would move to Thursday. Which should come first?”

Bring a realistic estimate, including time to check the work. If both deadlines really are fixed, ask what can change: “Could we reduce the report to the essential figures, or could someone take the first draft of the slides?”

Dorie Clark writes about protecting time for chosen priorities and leaving room between commitments. This is a LAiDIES script for making that trade-off visible at work. It will not manufacture extra hours, but it gives your manager a concrete decision to make.
